subject: Hiding original response data contained in a mirt model object

messages.author: 9c27ad9c7102c1c8
messages.subject: Hiding original response data contained in a mirt model object
parts:
Hi Phil, 

First, I want to thank you for all your incredible work developing mirt. 

We've been working to encourage folks to use pattern-based scoring more in their work with us. To accomplish this we've developed some very basic Shiny applications that take CSV files of responses and reference a mirt model object to use the mirt::fscore function to score the data. We want to pilot scaling this setup by developing the shiny app for clients to deploy locally with R-Studio. A complication in this workflow is that the mirt model object that comes from our finalized validation work contains the original response data. For some projects, these data are regulated and we are not permitted to share it. 

As such, we are wondering if there is a hack to hide the original response data contained inside a mirt model object, while still retaining the ability to use the mirt::fscore function? 

Thanks so much.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Hiding original response data contained in a mirt model object
parts:
Hi Brandon,

There probably is a way to hack at mirt's objects to hide all the data components, but I generally wouldn't recommend it. You might find the generate.mirt_object() function in the mirtCAT package more useful though as this effectively builds a mirt object for CATs using only the minimal object components. That would also give greater flexibility in case there are items you don't want included in the object, or if the ordering of the items should be modified for sequential scoring methods. HTH.

Phil
